Name: prepare_data.py
What it does: Pulls the latest data from TryBooking's S3 storage and rebuilds the local data warehouse that the dashboard and all reports read from.
Who receives it / Where output goes: Updates the dashboard automatically. No email sent.
How to run manually: python3 prepare_data.py — DuckDB only: python3 prepare_data.py --materialise-only
Technical notes: Builds SQLite (warehouse.db) and DuckDB (warehouse_duck.db). Runs weekends too — critical for month-end capture. Curls /api/warm after materialise. duckdb must be on PATH.

Name: s3_to_sharepoint.py
What it does: Copies TryBooking's raw data files from S3 into SharePoint so the team can access them directly.
How to run manually: python3 s3_to_sharepoint.py — preview without uploading: add --dry-run
Technical notes: ETag-based sync — only uploads changed files. Manifest at /root/s3reporting/.sync_manifest.

Name: zoho_industry.py
What it does: Keeps the Industry field in Zoho CRM up to date with the latest data from TryBooking.
Who receives it / Where output goes: Zoho CRM (field updates only — no email)
Technical notes: OAuth2 refresh token flow. Mon–Fri only.

Name: zoho_tiers.py
What it does: Recalculates which tier every account belongs to and updates Zoho CRM. Also updates the retention priority score used in the dashboard.
Who receives it / Where output goes: Zoho CRM (tier fields); CSV saved to reports/; dashboard updated by 03:30
Technical notes: Tier v2: 55% current 12m revenue + 35% lifetime + 10% years loyalty. Bands: T1 top 2%, T2 3–10%, T3 11–25%, T4 26–50%, T5 51–100%. Writes retention_priority to SQLite then triggers a second DuckDB materialise at 03:30.

Name: backup_to_sharepoint.py
What it does: Backs up the Pi's databases and config files to SharePoint every night in case of hardware failure.
Technical notes: Runs after the 03:30 materialise so the backup includes same-day data. Restore with restore_from_sharepoint.py.

Name: salesiq_weekly.py
What it does: Sends a summary of the week's Zoho SalesIQ chat activity to the team.
Technical notes: Pulls from Zoho SalesIQ API. Email via Azure Graph API. Runs 5 minutes before the accounts report.

Name: weekly_reporting_unified.py
What it does: Sends a report on new accounts signed up that week with year-on-year comparisons.
Who receives it / Where output goes: Email to stakeholders; CSV saved to reports/
How to run manually: python3 weekly_reporting_unified.py — to test without sending: export TEST_MODE=1 first
Technical notes: TEST_MODE redirects email to test recipients. TEST_DATE overrides the processing date. Email via Azure Graph API (Mailgun fallback).

Name: weekly_domain_report.py
What it does: Extracts the email domains of new users — useful for understanding acquisition channels.
Technical notes: Reads from the Users S3 report.

Name: monthly_reporting.py
What it does: Sends the monthly performance report covering the previous calendar month.
Who receives it / Where output goes: Email to stakeholders; CSV saved to reports/
Technical notes: S3 monthly files land on the 1st; new-month files appear on the 2nd — so the 1st always reads last month's data.

Name: sales_commission_report.py
What it does: Calculates and sends the monthly sales commission report for the sales team.
Who receives it / Where output goes: Email (PDF + HTML) to stakeholders; CSV saved to reports/
How to run manually: python3 sales_commission_report.py — to run for a specific month: export REPORT_MONTH=YYYY-MM first
Technical notes: Commission config (rates per person) in sales_commission_config.json. Email via Azure Graph API.

Name: eoy_planning_report.py
What it does: Generates detailed planning metrics — useful for target-setting, seasonality analysis, and year-end reviews. Covers revenue, cohorts, geography, industry, and keywords.
Who receives it / Where output goes: CSVs saved to planning/ seasonality/ industry/ cohorts/ geography/ keywords/
How to run manually: python3 eoy_planning_report.py — choose a mode: rolling / monthly_review / custom (set start+end dates)
Technical notes: Multiple output modes for different planning contexts. Requires GA4 credentials.

Name: industry_analysis.py
What it does: Breaks down accounts and revenue by industry — useful for sector-level reporting or presentations.
Technical notes: Reads BookingDataAll + BookingData + Accounts from S3.

Name: salesiq_monthly_report.py
What it does: Pulls a full year of monthly SalesIQ chat statistics — useful for annual reviews.
How to run manually: python3 salesiq_monthly_report.py — to choose a year: export YEAR=2025 first
Technical notes: Different from the weekly report — this is for historical analysis across a full year.

Name: ppc_reporting.py
What it does: Matches PPC ad clicks in Google Analytics with TryBooking sign-ups to show which campaigns are converting.
How to run manually: python3 ppc_reporting.py — to test: export TEST_MODE=1 first. Campaign config: config/ppc_campaigns.json
Technical notes: Data runs from 2024-06-01 to today. Requires GA4_PROPERTY_ID and GA4_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY.

Name: regional_segmentation.py
What it does: Shows the regional distribution of accounts and events across the UK based on postcodes.
Technical notes: Uses postcode areas to assign UK regions.

Name: analyse_wales_ni_sectors.py
What it does: Breaks down accounts in Wales and Northern Ireland by industry sector.
Technical notes: Subset of regional_segmentation.py focused on Wales and NI.

Name: keyword_analysis_report.py
What it does: Analyses event names to identify common types of events (e.g. balls, concerts, quiz nights) and how they trend over time.
Technical notes: Logic in modules/event_keyword_analysis.py.

Name: event_completion_reminders.py
What it does: Tags users in GetVero after their events complete so they receive automated follow-up messages.
Who receives it / Where output goes: Tags applied in GetVero; CSV audit trail saved locally
How to run manually: python3 event_completion_reminders.py — always test first: export TEST_MODE=1
Technical notes: TEST_MODE skips live Vero writes. API client: modules/utils/vero_api.py.

Name: funds_remaining_reminder.py
What it does: Tags users in GetVero who have funds remaining from past events so they can be reminded to use them.
Who receives it / Where output goes: Tags applied in GetVero; CSV audit trail saved locally
How to run manually: python3 funds_remaining_reminder.py — always test first: export TEST_MODE=1
Technical notes: TEST_MODE skips live Vero writes.

Name: pricing_scenarios_2026.py
What it does: Models what revenue would look like under different fee structures — online, Stripe, and box office card.
Who receives it / Where output goes: CSVs for each scenario saved to output/
Technical notes: Intended to be made generic for future years. Reads 2025 booking data as the baseline.

Name: pricing_model_comparison.py
What it does: Compares revenue outcomes across different pricing models side by side.
How to run manually: python3 pricing_model_comparison.py — to choose a year: export YEAR=2025 first
Technical notes: Use alongside pricing_scenarios_2026.py for full analysis.

Name: zoho_tiers_v2.py
What it does: Runs the tier calculation and shows what the results would be — without making any changes to Zoho CRM. Use this to check before running the live update.
Who receives it / Where output goes: CSV: tier_output.csv + summary printed to console
Technical notes: Dry run only — no Zoho writes.

Name: compare_tiers.py
What it does: Compares two sets of tier calculation results to highlight what has changed.
Technical notes: Run after zoho_tiers_v2.py to validate changes before going live.

Name: check_account_names.py
What it does: Takes a list of account names and fuzzy-matches them against TryBooking data — useful for identifying duplicates, merges, or looking up accounts by partial name.
Who receives it / Where output goes: CSV with matched / needs review / no match results
How to run manually: python3 check_account_names.py — requires a names.txt file in the working directory
Technical notes: Fuzzy matching — handles typos and partial names.

Name: account_box_office_cardpresent.py
What it does: Shows a breakdown of Box Office card-present revenue for a single account over the last 365 days.
Technical notes: Reads BookingData from S3.

Name: test_ppc_setup.py
What it does: Checks that AWS and Google Analytics credentials are correctly configured before running the PPC report.
Technical notes: Safe to run at any time — read-only.

Name: test_vero_api.py
What it does: Checks that the Vero API connection is working before running CRM action scripts.
Technical notes: Runs in test mode — no live writes.

Name: restore_from_sharepoint.py
What it does: Restores the Pi's databases and config from a SharePoint backup — used if the Pi fails or data is lost.
How to run manually: python3 restore_from_sharepoint.py --list to see available dates, then --date YYYY-MM-DD
Technical notes: Always run --list first. Restores from backups made by backup_to_sharepoint.py.
